summary: A sheet that slides in from an edge and keeps the page in view behind it: token details, filters, a review checklist. On touch it can be swiped away.
whenToUse: Details or editing for one item of a list or table, where the user wants to keep the list in mind.
Filters and settings for the current view.
side end (default) for details, start for navigation, bottom for small screens and quick choices.
whenNotToUse: A short task that needs full attention: use Dialog.
Content that should stay visible while the user works on the page: use a non-modal side panel in the layout.

dos.title: Title it with the item's name
dos.text: "color.signal.default" tells the user which row they opened. The description says what it is for.

dos.title: Put the actions in the footer
dos.text: The footer stays visible while the body scrolls.

donts.title: A drawer that opens another drawer
donts.text: Stacked sheets hide where the user came from. Navigate inside the drawer or use a page.

accessibility: Base UI Drawer: modal dialog semantics, named by the title, focus trapped, Escape closes, focus returns to the trigger.
Swipe to dismiss is an extra for touch, never the only way: the close button and Escape always work.
The page behind is inert while the drawer is open.
When the body is taller than the sheet it becomes a focusable region named by the title, so keyboard users can Tab to it and scroll with the arrow keys. A body that fits adds no tab stop.
Slides in 300ms with an exponential ease-out; reduced motion shows it instantly.
start and end follow the physical left and right in v1; RTL layouts should pass the mirrored side.
contentGuidelines: Title: the item's name, or the task when there is no item ("Filter tokens").
Footer: the same verb rules as Dialog. Primary last.
